DETAIL.NO_PHOTOS_YET: No photos yet. Upload one to keep a visual record of this tree.
DETAIL.PHOTOS_HINT: Photos are stored with Vercel Blob (JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF, up to 15 MB). When the file includes a camera capture date (EXIF), that date is used automatically; you can change it with the pencil control. You need a deployment with Blob and API routes configured.

DETAIL.ERROR_UPDATING_PHOTO_DATE: Could not update the photo date. Please try again.

EDIT_PHOTO_DATE_MODAL.TITLE: Photo date
EDIT_PHOTO_DATE_MODAL.DESCRIPTION: Set the date shown for this photo on {{treeName}} ({{fileName}}). When the file contains a camera date, it is filled in automatically on upload.
EDIT_PHOTO_DATE_MODAL.HINT: “Use upload date” removes a custom or EXIF date so the list shows when the photo was added to the app.

GOOGLE_PHOTOS_PICKER.TITLE: Select Photos from Google Photos
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_PICKER.DESCRIPTION: Choose photos from your Google Photos account to add to this bonsai tree
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_PICKER.NO_PHOTOS_DESC: No photos found in your Google Photos account
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_PICKER.SETUP_DESC: To use Google Photos, you need to set up the Google Photos API:
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_PICKER.SETUP_STEP_1: Enable the Google Photos Library API in Google Cloud Console
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_PICKER.SETUP_STEP_2: Add your Google Client ID to the environment variables
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_PICKER.SETUP_STEP_3: Grant the required permissions when prompted

GOOGLE_PHOTOS_SETUP.TITLE: Google Photos Setup Guide
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_SETUP.DESCRIPTION: To use Google Photos, you need to set up the Google Photos API in your Google Cloud Console.
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_SETUP.STEP_1_DESC: Go to Google Cloud Console and create a new project or select an existing one.
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_SETUP.STEP_2_DESC: Enable the Google Photos Library API in your project's API library.
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_SETUP.STEP_3_DESC: Create OAuth 2.0 credentials and add the client ID to your environment variables:
GOOGLE_PHOTOS_SETUP.STEP_4_DESC: After adding the environment variable, restart your development server.
